expectations.text: Frames a first dedicated platform hire at this company as a real resourcing shift rather than a routine backfill
expectations.evidence: The document treats the hires as a step up from the current setup. It says the API is 'run by two backend engineers part-time' and calls it a 'bolt-on public API'. The PM's mission is to 'Turn Calder's public REST API from an enterprise-driven side project into a product'. Under 'Sizing risk' it warns that 'three specialized hires on top of two part-time engineers is above that norm' and recommends gating one search. It never says outright that this is the company's first dedicated platform investment rather than a backfill, so the framing is only implied.

expectations.text: Any scorecard produced lists quantified outcomes rather than vague responsibilities such as owning the platform
expectations.evidence: All three scorecards list dated, numbered outcomes rather than duties. Examples: 'Day 60: an instrumented baseline is live', 'at least 10 interviews', 'at least 80% of committed roadmap items', 'active API accounts reach at least 2x the day-60 baseline', 'cut by at least 50% from the day-30 baseline', '99.9%' SLO, 'cut by 30% from baseline by day 180', 'at least 5 qualified partners... at least 2 live integrations'. Placeholder targets are marked *(proposed)*, and none of the outcomes reads like 'own the platform'.

expectations.text: Frames a first dedicated platform hire at this company as a real resourcing shift rather than a routine backfill
expectations.evidence: The transcript states that 'the two backend engineers stay on the API. These hires add product, architecture and partner capacity, and they don't replace those engineers.' The PM mission is to 'turn the REST API from an accommodation for three accounts into a product.' This separates the hires from a backfill and hints at a shift in how the API is resourced. It never says outright that these are the company's first dedicated platform roles, though, and it doesn't treat that as an organizational change with its own implications. The framing is implied, not developed.

expectations.text: Any scorecard produced lists quantified outcomes rather than vague responsibilities such as owning the platform
expectations.evidence: All three scorecards list ranked outcomes with deadlines (60/90 days, month 6/9/12) and concrete counts. Examples: 'at least 15 API consumers', '2 reference integrations', 'zero unannounced breaking changes', and 'monthly top-5 friction report'. Several key targets are unfilled placeholders, such as '[X]% of enterprise accounts', 'reduce interrupts by [X]%', '[baseline] to [target]' and '[N] partners'. Some outcomes are deliverables rather than measured results, such as 'publish API design standards'. The outcomes are concrete, but not fully quantified.
